A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MUDG work. The complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C are readable and support reliable matching despite substantial visual reformatting.

before.justification: v2 reports original retrieval experiments, MUDG classification results, ablations, simulations, and qualitative analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds coreset comparisons, a supervised reference, and qualitative retrieval and text-feature analyses.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2, adaptive augmentation, rank pseudo-labeling, clustering-based sample selection, and the diversity-preserving loss are unchanged. The new figures explain or evaluate the existing procedure rather than introduce method components.

E1.justification: Both versions use LAION-2B-en and the same 20 target benchmarks, including the appendix datasets. The added comparisons and diagnostics reuse existing coverage; the new e-commerce example is motivational, not an evaluated task.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds five ViT-B/16 coreset comparators: Margin, Least Confident, Entropy, Herding, and K-Ctr Greedy. It also adds a 16-shot supervised reference. This substantially expands the comparison methods while retaining the previous comparators in their corresponding experiments.

E3.justification: v3 adds a separate protocol that finetunes ViT-B/16 on 16-shot target training data. Figure 18 additionally samples 100 ImageNet class names for a text-feature comparison using augmentations with losses 0 and 16. Existing benchmark protocols and Tables 9–10 settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Figures 9–10 compare retrieval examples against SuS-X and examine retrieval failures. Appendix Figure 18 adds a t-SNE diagnostic of augmentation-induced feature contraction. These extend the existing qualitative analyses; the numerical component ablations and sensitivity studies are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages of three experiments or trials in Tables 2, 3, and 8. No changed run counts, seed reporting, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures are documented.

E6.justification: All matching numerical rows in Tables 2–8 are retained, but Table 2 adds a substantial comparison block across 11 datasets. Herding and K-Ctr Greedy report means of 70.9 and 70.5, versus the unchanged MUDG mean of 71.1. The new supervised reference averages 83.9 under different training conditions. Figures 9, 10, and 18 add qualitative findings.

T1.justification: Formal Assumptions 1–2, Theorems 1–2, Corollary 2, and the derivations and proofs in Appendix A are retained. The added conceptual and empirical illustrations do not introduce new mathematical results.

C1.justification: v3 removes the abstract's explicit assertion of no source–target relationship and qualifies the introduction by requiring source coverage of target visual concepts and their CLIP alignment. These boundaries already appeared in v2's limitations, making this a refinement of the main claim. The central retrieval and accuracy claims remain.

C2.justification: Figure 10 makes the existing alignment limitation concrete: it attributes failures for 'paddle' and 'clean room' to concept mismatch, and failures for 'playing Daf', 'lacelike', and 'silverbush' to inadequate alignment. The previous discussions of saturation, hubness, diversity, and overfitting remain.

D1.justification: v3 identifies Guo et al.'s DeepCore implementations as the source for the new coreset baselines and documents the setup of the added diagnostics. Existing implementation details, hardware costs, hyperparameter tables, and the code-access URL are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds Coleman et al. (2019), Guo et al. (2022), and Welling (2009), connecting the evaluation more directly to coreset selection. Sener and Savarese was already cited. The broader positioning against DG, SuS-X, retrieval augmentation, and modality-gap research remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The introduction gains an e-commerce example and revised problem framing, and its six-item contribution list becomes two core retrieval contributions. Citation style and conference headings change throughout, but most prose and the main section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds Figures 1, 9, 10, and 18, separates v2's combined overview into Figures 2–4, redraws several plots, expands Table 2, and places Tables 2–3 together. These substantially alter presentation. Figure 8 also introduces misleading accuracy axes: bars labeled 85.7 and 61.2 appear within an axis spanning 68–73.

improvement.justification: The added coreset comparisons and supervised reference strengthen the comparative context, while explicit source requirements and concrete failure cases clarify applicability. These provide a limited overall improvement. Figure 8's inconsistent accuracy axes are a presentation regression, but its numerical labels and the retained appendix tables preserve the underlying results.
